subject: Onramp subsidy proposal — staged credits + overage handling
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <emily@datafjord.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@datafjord.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Onramp subsidy proposal — staged credits + overage handling

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the time earlier today. Per our conversation I put together a concise onramp proposal for the POC/initial launch that balances your need to validate SKU-level usage with our objective of converting to a committed tier if the integration hits the expected volume. Attached: SOW_draft.pdf and credit_schedule_v1.xlsx (simple table with thresholds).

High level:
- Pilot length: 90 days (we can extend to 120 days if you need additional validation).
- Activation credit: $50k in credits to cover core ingestion and early tuning iterations.
- Staged credits: credits are released in two tranches: 60% at kickoff, 40% after the second month conditional on active usage (weekly heartbeat > 1k calls).
- Conversion path: if you sign a 6- or 12-month commit within 30 days of POC end, up to 50% of unused pilot credits can be applied as a one-time credit against the committed minimum in month 1.
- Per-token pricing guidance (hosted usage): we recommend a tiered discount schedule; details in the spreadsheet, but example: 0–250M tokens baseline, 250M–1B = 15% off, >1B = 25% off (flexible).
- Overage handling: during the pilot, overages draw down credits; post-conversion, overages invoice monthly with 30-day terms unless a prepaid tranche is negotiated.

Questions for you / ask:
1) Is a 90-day POC sufficient for your legal/engineering stakeholders?
2) Can procurement accept partial credit conversion into committed minimums?
3) Any constraints around invoicing cadence or purchase order templates we should know about?

If this looks reasonable I can have Ben draft a tightened credit schedule (we can add weekly gates and escrow language) and send a short DocuSign for the SOW. Would you like the first kickoff next Wednesday?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Director
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: SOW_draft.pdf (21 KB), credit_schedule_v1.xlsx (8 KB)

From: Emily Torres <emily@datafjord.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement <procurement@datafjord.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onramp subsidy proposal — staged credits + overage handling

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Quick clarifying questions from our side after reviewing with engineering and procurement:

- POC length: our standard is 90 days but engineering has asked whether we can front-load more credits in month 1 to cover heavy initial tuning (namely ingestion and fine-tuning loops). Is the 60/40 split configurable?
- Credits carryover: if we underutilize pilot credits, can those credits carry into month 1 of a paid commitment beyond the 50% convert rule? Procurement prefers a clear mechanism and hates exceptions.
- Overage: procurement wants to avoid surprise invoices. If overages will be invoiced monthly post-pilot, can we set an alert threshold and a cap (e.g., notify at 80% and cap billing at 150% of expected month unless pre-approved)?
- Accounting: we will need a sample invoice format and a one-page payment terms exhibit for our AP team.

Also looping our procurement lead in case they prefer to respond directly to the SOW language.

Best,
Emily Torres
Head of ML Platform
DataFjord
emily@datafjord.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Emily Torres <emily@datafjord.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement <procurement@datafjord.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Onramp subsidy proposal — staged credits + overage handling

Hi all —

Looping in a quick commercial suggestion to address Emily's procurement points. Short version: make the pilot predictable for DataFjord and defensible for Redwood.

Proposed refinements (credit_schedule_v2.xlsx attached):
- Front-loaded tranche option: 80% upfront / 20% conditional (can switch to 60/40 on request). Helps with the heavy initial tuning spend.
- Weekly gates: weekly activity heartbeat (>=1k calls/week) required to unlock the conditional tranche; we document exceptions for scheduled downtime.
- Credit carryover: allow unused pilot credits to be carried into the first paid month up to 30% (not to exceed the month 1 committed minimum). This is simpler than full carryover while giving procurement predictability.
- Overage guardrails: automated alerts at 75% and 90%; soft cap: billing estimate emailed at 120% with confirmation required before exceeding 150% of expected month. Post-pilot, overages invoice monthly with 30-day terms; if DFJ wants prepay protection we can structure a prepaid buffer.
- Discount bands (per-token hosted): example table in spreadsheet — baseline price, then multi-tier discounts by monthly token buckets (250M, 500M, 1B). For launch promo we can offer a temporary +5% across bands if a commit is signed within 45 days of pilot end.

Rationale: procurement needs clear deterministic mechanics; engineering gets more credits up front to iterate quickly; sales preserves a modest conversion incentive.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Marissa confirms which front-load split (80/20 or 60/40) DFJ prefers.
2) We add a one-page "payment terms exhibit" for AP (sample invoice format) and hand it to Emily's procurement.
3) If DFJ prefers, we can route the SOW through DocuSign with the launch promo clause active for Q1 signings.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call with procurement + engineering tomorrow afternoon.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

Attachments: credit_schedule_v2.xlsx (9 KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <emily@datafjord.ai>, procurement <procurement@datafjord.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Onramp subsidy proposal — staged credits + overage handling

Emily / Team —

Thanks — this is great feedback. To summarize a clean path forward so legal/AP can move quickly: 

Agreed pilot mechanics:
- Pilot length: 120 days (we agreed to extend to give additional validation).
- Credits: $50k activation + staged release. DFJ chose 80% upfront / 20% conditional (Ben's suggestion).
- Carryover: unused pilot credits may carry into month 1 of a paid commitment up to 30% of month 1 committed minimum.
- Overage guardrails: alerts at 75/90%, billing estimate at 120% and no charge beyond 150% without written approval.
- Conversion incentive: sign a 6- or 12-month commit within 45 days of pilot end to receive an extra 5% lift on discount bands (applies first three billed months).

Action items:
- Marissa: update SOW to reflect 120-day pilot, insert carryover clause and the alert/cap language; push to DocuSign by Monday.
- Ben: include one-page payment terms exhibit and a sample invoice (AP-friendly).
- Emily / procurement: confirm PO template or any unusual AP fields we should populate in the DocuSign packet.

Proposed kickoff: 2027-02-17 @ 10:00 PT for implementation + engineering t-shirt sizing (30 min). If that works I'll lock it and send calendar invites.

If procurement is happy I'll route the SOW through DocuSign with the launch promo clause active (DFJ qualifies for the Q1 launch promo if they sign within the window).

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales Director
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
